subject: physics
title: Electricity & Magnetism Adventure 1: Coulomb's law and electric fields
welcome_lead: Today you'll feel Coulomb's force and map electric fields.
meta_desc: Physics — Coulomb's law, electric field E, potential V, parallel plates.
final_note: You learned F = kq₁q₂/r², E = F/q, V = work/q, between parallel plates E = V/d.

walkthroughs.body_html:
F = k · q₁ · q₂ / r²

k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N m²/C².
Same sign → repulsion. Opposite → attraction.

1 C is a huge charge: two 1 C charges 1 m apart push with 9 × 10⁹ N. Realistic charges are nC or μC.

E = F/q (N/C). Field lines from + to −.

Point charge: E = kQ/r².

Electric potential V (scalar): work done per unit charge from infinity. V = kQ/r for point.

Equipotentials ⊥ field lines.

Uniform field between plates: E = V/d.

V volts, d metres, E in V/m.

Cathode ray tube: deflect electron beam.
Capacitor stores energy ½ CV² (HL).

Lightning: huge V between cloud and ground; air dielectric breaks down at ~3 × 10⁶ V/m.
